title: Prefill scheduler: quantization cost amortizer for hybrid INT8/FP8 kernels
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Reduce end-to-end decode cost and tail latency for medium-length workloads by amortizing dequantization overhead across prefill and decode phases. We will implement a scheduler that negotiates hybrid kernel selection (INT8 fast path vs FP8 fallback) at microbatch boundaries and coalesces dequant operations where safe. The feature targets cases where token distribution and KV-cache reuse make dequant overhead non-trivial (multi-turn chat with 1k-4k context). Constraints: must preserve numerical stability for attention and logits, minimal additional memory per request, and be compatible with streaming outputs and function-calling cases.
acceptance_criteria: p50 decode latency improvement >= 8% for 1024-token prefills on A100 under representative trace
p99 decode latency regression <= 2% vs current baseline across heavy concurrency (>=64 concurrent streams)
token-level cost reduction >= 12% for hybrid INT8/FP8 candidate models in our benchmark suite
fallback correctness validated: output logit diffs within tolerance for 99.9% of test prompts
new scheduler passes integration tests and includes storybook traces in Console rollout view
comments: 2025-02-14 - Maya Chen: Created ticket after measurement spike on dequant hotspots. Attached initial microbench traces and representative production query samples.

2025-02-18 - Diego Martinez: Spike prototype implemented: 'dequant-coalesce' stage that merges adjacent per-layer dequant ops during prefill. Preliminary microbench shows ~9% p50 improvement on 1.5k token runs, but p99 unchanged.
2025-02-21 - Aisha Patel (review): Concern around streaming: merging dequant across prefill may add jitter when latency SLOs are tight for early tokens. Suggested gated rollout and telemetry flag.

2025-02-26 - Diego Martinez: Ran ablation contrasting three strategies: immediate-dequant (baseline), coalesced-prefill, and deferred-dequant-on-decode. Coalesced-prefill best for cost, deferred-dequant sometimes improves p99 at expense of cost. Added hybrid negotiator that picks strategy per-request.
2025-03-01 - PM review (Liam O'Connor): Prioritize canary for dedicated customers with SLA. Add dashboard to show per-request chosen strategy and cost delta.

2025-03-04 - Diego Martinez: Merged kernel-selector and scheduler prototype into feature branch. Running 48h canary on dedicated pool with synthetic multi-turn traffic. Observed token cost down ~13% and p50 down ~12%; investigating two outlier queries causing p99 spikes.
observations: Dequantization overhead is not uniformly distributed: layers with headwise scale and per-head reproject add the most CPU/GPU prep time
Microbatch alignment wins: when prefill microbatches share KV layout, a single fused dequant op gives amortized benefits
FP8 fallback is stable for attention matmuls but causes subtle distribution shifts in final logits for certain normalization ordering
Hybrid negotiator that uses simple heuristics (context length, recent cache-hit rate, concurrency) gives >80% of ideal oracle cost savings in tests
decisions: Implement per-request negotiator returning one of: INT8-fused-prefill, FP8-fallback-immediate, Deferred-dequant-on-decode
Expose per-request strategy in telemetry and allow Console rollout gating per-customer
Add microbench harness to compare kernel variants across sequence lengths and batch sizes before releasing
Keep default conservative for streaming low-latency tier: prefer deferred-dequant to avoid early-token jitter
next_steps: Stabilize fallback correctness tests (unit + 50k example prompts) and add logit-diff regression alert
Finish Graphviz of scheduler decision path and add to Confluence design doc
Instrument Console to show chosen strategy and cost delta per route for canary customers
Coordinate with SRE to schedule capacity for canary 72h run and monitor p99 anomalies
Prepare rollout plan for runtime-1.20 with feature flag default OFF for hosted but ON for selected Dedicated tenants
